Plain-English guide

The Texas buyer agreement, explained in 3 minutes

Since Jan 1, 2026, Texas buyers sign a written agreement with their agent. Here's what's in it and what to negotiate.

Find your agent in 2 minutes

The 5 lines that matter

  • Type: showing-only (non-exclusive, ≤14 days) or full representation
  • Fee: the % or flat amount your agent earns
  • Who pays: whether the agent will seek it from the seller/builder first
  • Term: how long you're committed — shorter is safer
  • Termination: how either side can end it
Money Move tip: start with a showing-only agreement. If you love your agent, sign the full one. If not, text "swap."
Do I have to sign an agreement with a buyer's agent in Texas?

Yes. Since January 1, 2026 (SB 1968), a Texas agent needs a written agreement before performing brokerage services for a buyer. You can start with a showing-only agreement that is non-exclusive and lasts 14 days or less.

Who pays the buyer's agent?

It's negotiable. Your agreement states the fee. Sellers and builders often agree to pay some or all of it as a concession, and a good agent asks for that in your offer. Anything they don't cover, you owe — so read that line.

Can I get out of a buyer agreement?

Depends on the terms you sign. Look for a short term and a clear termination clause. Our partner agents agree to let Money Move clients end the agreement early if it isn't working.

Not legal advice. Sources: Texas SB 1968 (89R) bill analysis; Texas REALTORS agency law explainer.
